newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt down in quiet trade amid Mexico peso woes.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt down in quiet trade amid Mexico peso woes.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices slipped in quiet afternoon trade as a drop in the Mexican currency pressured the market, traders said.
"More than anything, the market is down because of weakness in the peso," said one emerging markets debt trader at a major U.S. investment bank.
One source said news Sunday that the Mexican government would not privitize 100 percent of its petrochemical plants triggered the drop in the peso and subsequent fall in the emerging debt markets.

"The economy is doing very well but news over the weekend that the government is not going to be able to privitize the majority stakes in petrochemicals was a bit of a negative," the emerging market debt source noted.
At 1530 EDT/1930 GMT, Mexico's global bonds due 2026 were 1-1/4 weaker at 99-7/8 bid and the country's par bonds were 5/8 softer at 69-5/8 bid.
Trading sources said, however, that activity remained thin ahead of key U.S. inflation figures due out later in the week.

"I think that the (U.S. Treasury) bond market is being very benign," one said. "There are some inflation numbers due out tomoorrow and the rest of the week, so it is fairly slow. There is not a lot of trading going on."
On Wednesday, the U.S. Labor Department will release the September consumer price index.
In the broader market, Brazil's "C" bonds were 7/8 lower at 71-5/8 bid and Venezuelan DCBs were 7/8 weaker at 83-3/8.
Meanwhile, emerging market debt sources said a spate of new issues are awaiting pricing.

Joint lead managers J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg said last week in London that the roadshow for Brazil's $750 million global bond issue will be held during the week starting October 21 and presentations will be made in Asia, Europe and the United States.
Also awaiting issuance is Russia's Eurobond issue.
Among Eastern European debt issues, Russian Vnesh dollar debt were 7/8 lower at 78-1/8 bid and Bulgarian FLRB's were 1/8 weaker at 32 bid.
